SOURCE: "Deep Think with Confidence" (DeepConf), Yichao Fu, Xuewei Wang, Yuandong Tian, Jiawei Zhao (Meta AI, UCSD). arXiv:2508.15260v1, 21 Aug 2025. It is a preprint with no venue printed.

COVERAGE: I read all 84,865 chars of the extraction: main text, Tables 1-12, ablations, appendices A-G and references. In Appendix G (vLLM edit snippets) I read the setup and the API call and skimmed the copy-paste code. Table 10 and the fine text of Figs 8, 9 and 11 (the per-model curves) are figure data and were not extracted. Page numbers are from the figure captions tool and the text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Confidence-filtered voting beats plain majority voting on hard math, with the largest gain from keeping the top 10% of traces.
  number: DeepSeek-8B AIME25 82.3 to 87.4; Qwen3-32B AIME24 85.3 to 90.8; GPT-OSS-120B AIME25 97.0 (cons@512) to 99.9
  setup: K=512 traces, offline, 64 resamples from a pool of 4,096 traces per problem. Open-weight models only (Table 1).
  quote: "Filtering with η=10% yields the largest gains, with notable improvements like DeepSeek-8B on AIME25 (82.3%→ 87.4%) and Qwen3-32B on AIME24 (85.3% → 90.8%); GPT-OSS-120B even reaches 99.9% on AIME25."
  where: p8, section 4.2
- Online early stopping cuts generated tokens by large amounts at the same accuracy.
  number: up to 84.7% fewer tokens; DeepConf-low saves 43-79% and DeepConf-high 18-59% on the sets in the main text
  setup: Budget 512, Ninit=16 warmup traces, consensus τ=0.95, window 2,048 tokens. DeepSeek-8B, Qwen3-32B and GPT-OSS-120B on AIME24, AIME25, BRUMO25 and HMMT25 (Table 2). GPT-OSS-120B AIME25 went from 3.23e8 to 0.49e8 tokens.
  quote: "Compared with the majority voting baseline, DeepConf-low reduces tokens by 43-79% across AIME24/AIME25/BRUMO25/HMMT25." Also "reduces generated tokens by up to 84.7% compared to full parallel thinking."
  where: p1 abstract; p9-10, Table 2
- Cost of plain majority voting is steep.
  number: 511 extra traces and 100M extra tokens per question for a 68% to 82% gain
  setup: Qwen3-8B, AIME 2025
  quote: "improving pass@1 accuracy from 68% to 82% using standard majority voting on AIME 2025 requires 511 additional reasoning traces per question using Qwen3-8B, consuming 100 million additional tokens."
  where: p2
- Aggressive filtering can hurt when the model is "confidently wrong". Top-90% is the safe setting.
  number: top-10% improved 12 of 20 settings (+0.26 to +9.38 points) and dropped on 8 (-4.69 to -0.31), with an average gain of +1.22. Top-90% moved -0.21 to +0.73, average +0.17.
  setup: Lowest-group-confidence filter, 5 model configs by 4 datasets, voting size 1-512 (Appendix C).
  quote: "These regressions arise from rare cases where confidence concentrates on an incorrect answer (“confidently wrong”)."
  where: p19, Appendix C
- Local confidence signals (tail, bottom, lowest group) separate correct from incorrect traces better than a trace-wide mean. Confidence from the first tokens has no signal.
  number: averages over 23 model-dataset pairs at K=512 with a 10% filter: Tail(10%)@10 84.6, Tail(2k)@10 84.5, LGC(2k)@10 84.4, Mean@10 83.9, plain majority 83.0. Head(10%)@10 scored 81.9.
  setup: Offline, 5 models by up to 5 datasets (Tables 6-9).
  quote: "Across models and datasets, head-based confidence has weak correlation with final correctness and typically matches plain majority voting; applying head-based filters even hurts on average"
  where: p18-19, Appendix B.4
- The consensus-stopping threshold is a tunable trade-off.
  number: τ=0.95 saved 52.8% of tokens (DeepConf-low) and 54.7% (DeepConf-high) at B=512 with no accuracy loss. τ=0.85 reached up to 69.6% savings, but DeepConf-low lost 0.31 to 0.47 points.
  setup: Qwen3-32B, AIME24 (Table 3)
  quote: "τ =0.95 achieves optimal balance: it preserves accuracy exactly while saving 15.4%/52.8% tokens at B = 32/512 (DeepConf-low) and 22.0%/54.7% (DeepConf-high)."
  where: p17
- Filtering helps less or fails on some model-dataset pairs, and top-10% can lose to plain voting.
  number: Qwen3-8B AIME25 Top10 77.9 vs majority 82.6; GPT-OSS-120B HMMT25 online DeepConf-low 92.0 vs 92.8; Qwen3-32B BRUMO25 -0.9
  setup: Tables 2 and 5. Appendix D lists nine DeepConf-low settings and one DeepConf-high setting where matched accuracy at lower tokens was not achieved.
  quote: "several exceptions exist within the B ∈ [32, 512] range where matching majority voting accuracy with reduced token consumption is not achieved"
  where: p9, p23
- GPQA-Diamond (graduate-level STEM questions, not competition math) gains are small.
  number: about 6% over a single trace; Table 1 DeepSeek-8B 72.5 (cons) to 74.0 (best), but 70.6 for Bottom-10%@10
  setup: DeepSeek-8B, Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B, offline
  quote: "both variants provide clear average improvements of approximately 6%."
  where: p23, Appendix E
- Larger warmup moves online accuracy closer to the offline result, with a default of 16.
  number: |ΔAcc| across warmup sizes is typically ≤1.0 point
  setup: Ninit 8, 16 and 32 (Table 4)
  quote: "Empirically, |∆Acc| across warm-up sizes is small (typically ≤ 1.0 p.p.)."
  where: p17

DEFINITIONS (verbatim, for a code or explanation snippet)
- "Token Confidence. We define token confidence Ci as the negative average log-probability of the top-k tokens at position i" (p3)
- Group confidence is the mean token confidence over a sliding window of n previous tokens (n = 1024 or 2048).
- Bottom-10% group confidence is the mean of the lowest 10% of group confidences in a trace.
- Tail confidence is the mean over the last 2,048 tokens.
- The online stopping threshold is s = Percentile(100−η) of the warmup traces' confidence. A trace stops when its current group confidence falls below s.
- Consensus β = V(â) / ΣV(a). Sampling stops when β ≥ τ or the budget B is reached.

LIMITS
- The method needs token log-probabilities (top_logprobs ≥ 2) and a hook in the serving stack. The authors patched vLLM (a pinned commit), and the early-stop check is "inactive unless logprobs=True and top_logprobs>=2". Closed APIs that hide logprobs cannot use it. This is not a prompting technique.
- Only five open-weight models were tested: DeepSeek-8B (R1-0528 distilled into Qwen3-8B), Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-32B, GPT-OSS-20B and GPT-OSS-120B. Four are competition-math sets (AIME24, AIME25, BRUMO25, HMMT25). The one non-math set is GPQA-Diamond. Answers are extracted from `\boxed{}`, so the tasks have checkable final answers. Open-ended tasks are not tested.
- The authors concede model overconfidence: "addressing cases where models exhibit high confidence on incorrect reasoning paths, which is a key limitation observed in our experiments." No calibration fix is offered.
- GPT-OSS-20B and Qwen3-8B often gain nothing or lose. The headline 99.9% and 84.7% are best cases on GPT-OSS-120B AIME25.
- Results average 64 resamples from a fixed pool of 4,096 traces per problem, not fresh generations. Token counts include only traces generated before early stopping.
- The "no additional training or hyperparameter tuning" claim in the abstract sits alongside tuned choices: η, τ, Ninit and the window size. Each problem also needs 16 full warmup traces.
- Decoding settings were fixed: temperature 0.6 for DeepSeek-8B and Qwen3, 1.0 for GPT-OSS. GPT-OSS ran at reasoning effort high.
- Dated: models and benchmarks are from mid-2025.
- Nothing is said about prompt wording beyond the single instruction below.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Self-consistency with majority voting (Wang et al., 2023).
- Self-certainty and confidence-based best-of-n (Kang et al., 2025), which the paper calls the "global confidence" baseline.
- Early-stopping and adaptive voting: Dynamic Voting (Xue et al., 2023), Early-Stopping Self-Consistency (Li et al., 2024), Adaptive-Consistency (Aggarwal et al., 2023), Reasoning-Aware SC (Wan et al., 2025) and Dynasor (Fu et al., 2024).
- Token-level uncertainty (Fadeeva et al., 2024; Geng et al., 2024).
- It cites Chen et al. 2024b (arXiv:2412.21187) for efficient-CoT fine-tuning, which is in the target note. It also cites Jaech et al. 2024 (arXiv:2412.16720, the o1 system card) as a model reference. Both are already in the note's sources.
- Hassid et al. 2025 (shorter chains preferred), Snell et al. 2024 and Brown et al. 2024 (repeated sampling).

CODE
- Appendix G.3 enables the early stop through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (p25):
```
responses = client.chat.completions.create(
 model=args.model_path, messages=messages, max_tokens=args.max_tokens,
 temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95, logprobs=True, top_logprobs=20, n=real_gen,
 extra_body={"top_k": 0, "vllm_xargs": {"enable_conf": True, "window_size": 2048, "threshold": conf_threshold}})
```
- Fig 1 shows pseudocode: after each token, compute the group confidence `gc`, then "If gc >= threshold: continue generation else: stop generation".
- Algorithm 2 (p7) is a clean pseudo-spec of the online procedure.
- Prompt (Appendix F): "Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}." This is the prompt used for Qwen3 and GPT-OSS. This is relevant to the note's "drop step-by-step CoT" advice. The paper does not test whether the sentence matters.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p1): top, accuracy bars for AIME25 (pass@1, cons@512, deepconf@512) and tokens saved. Bottom, a token-by-token confidence trace with the stop rule. It is the best single summary.
- Fig 3 (p5): confidence measures plus weighted voting. A worked example has trace votes 17/15/13/11/9, filtering to the top 10%, and weights (17+13)/2.
- Fig 4 (p6): online stopping against the warmup threshold.
- Fig 2 (p3): confidence histograms for correct vs incorrect traces on HMMT25 (30 problems, 4,096 traces each). It shows why tail and bottom-10% separate better than the mean.
- Fig 6/7 (p10): tokens and accuracy against token cost.
- Fig 5/8/9: accuracy against voting budget curves (offline and online).

RELEVANCE TO NOTE 07
It extends the note's pass@k and verifier-free passage. The note says "none of it helps without a verifier... You can only vote". DeepConf is a verifier-free selector that is better than a plain vote, but it needs logprobs and open weights. It is also the same constraint the note gives for Ma et al.: it works only where you control the serving stack. It sets a budget-aware counterpart to the note's overthinking row. The note's "Real samples are correlated" caveat is consistent with the 'confidently wrong' failure here.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found.
- The extraction of Fig 1 text is garbled with interleaved axis labels, but the numbers match Table 1/2. Math symbols are mangled in equations, so eq. numbers are given by label only.
- Table 10 and the data in Figs 8, 9 and 11 were not extracted, so I did not quote them.
- The abstract says "99.9% accuracy" and "up to 84.7%". These come from two different configurations: offline tail confidence, and online DeepConf-low (Table 2: 97.9% accuracy at 84.7% fewer tokens). Do not combine them in one sentence.
- Table 2 DeepConf-low AIME24 DeepSeek-8B is 92.5% accuracy, while Table 4 reports the same cell as 92.5% against an offline 93.3%. These are consistent.
- Fig 6's text says "up to 85.8%" while Table 2 says 84.7% for the same model. This is an inconsistency inside the paper (p9).
